newsitem.title: UK: British Gas breaks contract logjam.
newsitem.headline: British Gas breaks contract logjam.

text.p: British Gas Plc on Thursday claimed a breakthrough in its efforts to renegotiate crippling "take-or-pay" contracts which oblige it to buy more gas than it can sell.
The company, which also announced its planned demerger is to take place in February, said it reached a deal with British Petroleum, which will cut the burden on British Gas.

British Gas struck a similar deal with its internal gas production arm, which sells gas to its supply business, and said it would pay total compensation of 293 million pounds ($476 million) to both its production unit and BP.
The take-or-pay contracts with various North Sea gas producers were signed when British Gas, privatised in 1986, still a national monopoly.
But the market for big industrial gas users was opened up to competition in the early 1990s, and British Gas has since seen its market share slump while the spot gas price has fallen.
The contracts, many of which stretch over decades, proved a massive burden for British Gas, which took a provision of 520 million pounds for the deal late in 1995.
The utility has since been trying to strike softer deals with its numerous gas suppliers, including such giants as Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Amerada Hess.
British Gas said the agreement with BP could be a stepping stone to similar deals.

"The deal with BP... and the agreement with BG's exploration and production business are vitally important first signs of progress," Roy Gardner, chief executive designate of the group's gas trading arm, told a news conference.

British Gas said the two deals represented about 10 percent of the gas volume it wants to tackle through contract renegotiations. Analysts said they believed British Gas was also about to conclude talks with Mobil.

Separately British Gas said it would seek shareholder approval for its proposed demerger on February 12. The demerger was first announced in February and was originally scheduled to take place next spring.
"I am delighted to be able to bring forward the demerger timetable," chairman Richard Giordano said.
"Even the privatisation in 1986 did not fundamentally change the structure of the organisation to the degree that the demerger obviously will," he added.
British Gas will float off a new company, called Centrica, to handle its gas trading business together with its gas fields off northwest England.
The rest of British Gas will be renamed BG Plc and will comprise the Transco gas transportation and storage business along with BG's exploration and production activities.
Shareholders will receive one Centrica share for every British Gas share held. Centrica shares are expected to start trading on February 17.
The planned split into two will help the trouble-hit company by allowing two sets of management to concentrate on their own problems, Giordano said.

BG's initial problem is about regulatory proposals for a tough new pricing regime. The price plans are currently being vetted by the British Monopolies and Mergers Commission after being rejected by British Gas. Centrica's problems include the take-or-pay contracts.
British Gas shares initially jumped on news of the take-or-pay breakthrough, but then retreated to close up 4-1/2 pence at 218-1/2 amid wariness over BG's 1997 dividend.
"You've got to acknowledge there is a possibility that the dividend will be halved," said Daniel Martin, analyst at BZW. ($1=.6161 Pound)
